subject: Triaging retention variance & BYOK evidence for Akron Medical (Private)
messages:
From: Helen Su <helen.su@akronmed.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@auditeq.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: retention variance & BYOK evidence for Private deployment - Akron Medical

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams reviewed the Private deployment spec and we have two urgent asks before we can sign the PO: 1) a retention variance to 30 days (default is 180 days) for prompt/response logs containing PHI; and 2) documentary evidence and sample audit exports showing BYOK/KMS usage and key access events (we need to show that customer-managed keys are used and that key material is never stored by Redwood).

Specifically we need:
- A short attestation or sample report that shows KMS key creation/rotation and access logs: who/what used the key and timestamps.
- A sample audit export with decryption/access events and the format/schema.
- Confirmation of what we can set as retention parameters for logs and backups, and whether we can enforce a 30-day TTL across all logs and cached data for the tenant.

Can we get a small evidence bundle and a short call this week to triage? AuditEQ (cc'd) will be handling evidence ingestion.

Best,
Helen Su
Head of IT Security
Akron Medical

Attachments: akron_poc_requirements.pdf (PDF)
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: Helen Su <helen.su@akronmed.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention variance & BYOK evidence for Private deployment - Akron Medical

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear list. Posting here so we can triage internally and respond with a concrete plan. High-level responses up front:

- Retention: we can support per-tenant log retention down to 30 days in Private (there are a couple of caveats for backups & cold archives). We need to confirm whether any debug/diagnostic traces are in scope.
- BYOK evidence: we can generate sample KMS access logs and an example audit export. Note that some of the key material/metadata is from the cloud KMS provider (if using cloud KMS) and will include provider-specific fields. For HSM-on-prem we can provide an attestation template.

Action items I propose:
1) Karthik: produce a small sample audit export (redwood-byo-log-sample.json) and list any provider fields we cannot redact.
2) Neha: confirm SOC2/control mapping for the evidence we provide and whether we need a formal exception or signed attestation.
3) Mina: run through retention config edge cases (backups, metrics, cached prefix) and note any technical blockers.
4) Connor: own the customer call and timeline (Helen, when are you available?)

Helen — can we book 45 minutes Wednesday or Thursday morning PT? I can circulate an MA-plan and a short evidence bundle ahead of the call.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, Helen Su <helen.su@akronmed.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention variance & BYOK evidence for Private deployment - Akron Medical

Evelyn/Helen — quick technical note from the infra side. I attached a tiny synthetic sample (redwood-byo-log-sample.json) showing the shape of the audit export. Highlights:

- What we can provide today: KMS key usage events (create, decrypt/encrypt, rotate), timestamp, principal id (redacted service account id for cross-tenant safety), and request metadata (IP, region).
- What we cannot provide from Redwood: raw key material (we never export that), and some cloud-provider-only fields (e.g., cloud KMS internal operation ids) may not be present in our normalized audit export. We can include provider ids on request but we'd need an NDA amendment in a few cases.
- Retention: we can set tenant-level retention for the audit stream to 30 days. However:
  * Backups: we keep rolling snapshots for 90 days by default; for a true 30-day hard-delete we'd need a policy exception and a runbook to scrub older snapshots (possible on Dedicated/Private with operator help).
  * Cached KV entries (prefix caching) live in hot memory and are evicted; we can guarantee that no persisted cache exceeds 30 days but ephemeral traces may remain in logs for investigative debugging unless suppressed.

Proposal: produce the sample export + an operator runbook for the backup-scrub step and a short technical appendix listing provider fields and limits.

- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-byo-log-sample.json (sample)
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, Helen Su <helen.su@akronmed.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention variance & BYOK evidence for Private deployment - Akron Medical

Thanks — adding compliance context. A few items we need answered before we can sign-off on an exception or formal variance:

1) Scope: confirm which data classes are in-scope for the 30-day request (prompts only, prompts+responses, system logs, debug traces).
2) Emergency restore: does Akron require the ability to restore beyond 30 days for legal hold? If so, we need a documented legal-hold workflow.
3) Attestation: AuditEQ will ingest our output; we can provide an attestation template but legal will need to review.

I recommend:
- We provide the sample export and the technical appendix (Karthik), and a short SOC2 control map showing which controls the evidence maps to (I will prepare).
- For the backup-scrub runbook: we draft an operator playbook and a small change request for Private customers to allow a certified scrub (Connor to own the operational runbook).

Helen — can you confirm scope (item #1) and whether you need a legal-hold path (item #2)? If both yes, expect a ~2 week turnaround on a consolidated evidence bundle + runbook and a separate timeline for any contract amendment.

- Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: Helen Su <helen.su@akronmed.com>

Subject: Re: Request: retention variance & BYOK evidence for Private deployment - Akron Medical

Helen — thanks for the quick responses and to AuditEQ for joining. Based on the notes above, here is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) for the trial and POC evidence collection:

1) This week: Connor will schedule a 45-minute triage with your team to confirm scope (prompts only vs full transcript) and legal-hold requirements. Please choose between Wed 09/03 10:00 or Thu 09/04 09:00 PT.
2) Karthik: deliver sample audit export + technical appendix by Fri 09/04.
3) Neha: deliver SOC2 control map and attestation template by Tue 09/08.
4) Mina & Connor: draft the backup-scrub runbook and operational checklist for a 30-day hard-delete on Private by Tue 09/08.
5) After MAP items are delivered, AuditEQ will validate the bundle and confirm whether any additional provider fields are required for their ingestion.

We will treat the backup-scrub as an operational exception scoped to Akron's tenant; if legal-hold or other constraints require, we'll follow an approved process for temporary restores. If any contract amendments are required, we will flag for the commercial team.

Helen — if that looks good I will mark Connor as the POC and circulate calendar invites after you confirm a meeting slot.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
